remaining: Alpha Bank Cyprus current ATM/self-service counts; identity of the new external ATM monitoring/disputes provider; Alpha careers/job-ad angle for AML+self-service roles; any 2026 statement on next strategic plan / Investor Day; Printec case-study archive (Wayback) for the Siron implementation citation.

signals.signal: First hard ATM fleet count from a primary audited source: 1,199 ATMs in Greece at 31/12/2025 (1,193 at 31/12/2024). During 2025, 262 network-optimisation studies produced 15 new off-site ATMs; the ATM network kept transaction volumes stable. 98% of the branch network has at least one Automated Payment System (APS).
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025 (Board of Directors' Report, ESRS metrics Table 63)
signals.implies: Sizes the addressable Alpha self-service estate at ~1,200 ATMs plus ~240 APS kiosks - hardware refresh, recycler upgrade, software licensing and managed services all scale off this number. The 15 net-new off-site placements show an expanding, not shrinking, off-site footprint (unlike NBG).
signals.likelihood: Continuous - annual site studies already institutionalised
signals.followup: Ask Alpha for the in-branch vs off-site and deposit-capable vs withdrawal-only split; benchmark against NBG 1,360 and Piraeus c.1,500.

signals.signal: Voice-guidance (audio navigation for blind/partially sighted users) runs on only 300 of 1,199 ATMs (~25%), versus 299 of 1,193 a year earlier. The report states that more than 1,100 Alpha ATMs already have the hardware sockets for the service and that the constraint is purely licensing: the Bank holds exactly 300 software licences and 'the number of ATMs providing this service will increase with the approval of the purchase of additional software licences.' Alpha has also initiated a coordinated accessibility programme for WCAG 2.2 AA / EU Accessibility Act compliance.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, footnote 56 to Table 63 and 'Inclusive access to products and services'
signals.implies: A named, quantified, hardware-ready upsell of ~800-900 additional voice-guidance software licences plus deployment services on an estate where Printec is the incumbent voice-guidance supplier. Peer pressure is explicit: NBG had 837 voice ATMs at end-2025 targeting 100% by end-2026 and Eurobank claims 100%, so Alpha at 25% is the sector laggard with an accessibility-regulation deadline behind it.
signals.likelihood: High within 6-12 months - the only gate named is internal purchase approval
signals.followup: Take a costed 900-licence proposal (plus phased rollout services) to Alpha's Self-Service / Accessibility owners, framed on the EU Accessibility Act and the NBG/Eurobank 100% benchmark.

signals.signal: During 2025 Alpha entered 'a new partnership with a specialised external provider for ATM Monitoring and Disputes Resolution services', lifting ATM network availability to over 97% (+1.1 percentage points vs 2024). The provider is not named.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, 'ATM Network & Automated Payment Systems'
signals.implies: Alpha is actively buying ATM managed services (monitoring, availability management, dispute/chargeback handling) from third parties - exactly Printec's managed-services line. If the incumbent is a competitor this is a displacement target; if it is Printec it is an expansion reference. Availability at 'over 97%' is still below the 98%+ SLA class Printec sells, leaving headroom to bid on an improvement target.
signals.followup: Identify the provider (Alpha procurement/DORA third-party register, LinkedIn, Greek IT press) and quantify the availability gap to a 99% SLA.

signals.signal: Siron Embargo is confirmed by primary disclosure as Alpha Bank's sanctions-screening tool: in 2025 the Bank 'optimised' it by introducing dual-control functionality for transactions meeting specific risk-based criteria, integrated new high-risk factors into its customer risk-rating methodology, and aligned AML platforms and core banking with the SEPA Instant Payments Regulation. A comprehensive GAP analysis against the new EU AML package (AMLR/AMLD6/AMLA) with initial action plans was due to complete by Q2 2026. Siron itself is no longer a FICO product: IMTF completed the acquisition of the entire Siron Compliance & AML business from FICO, announced 12/01/2022, taking over all Siron products, staff and client contracts worldwide.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025 (AML/CFT actions) + IMTF press release
signals.implies: Confirms the Siron estate is live and being actively invested in, and pins the vendor relationship on IMTF rather than FICO - a partner/channel question Printec must settle before selling into it. The AMLR gap analysis finishing in Q2 2026 is the classic trigger for a transaction-monitoring/screening replacement or augmentation programme, which is Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring line.
signals.likelihood: High - AMLR applies 10/07/2027, remediation budgets set in 2026-27
signals.followup: Confirm Printec's current channel position on Siron under IMTF ownership, then request the AMLR gap-analysis remediation backlog from Alpha's AML/CFT Business Area.

signals.signal: A NEW Voluntary Exit Scheme was approved by the Executive Committee on 14/01/2026 with an estimated cost of EUR 44 million and estimated participation of 350 employees, and the programme was completed on 30/01/2026. Branch estate at 31/12/2025 (audited): 270 Group branches, of which 244 in Greece and 26 abroad.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, 'Number of Branches' and 'Events after the balance sheet date'
signals.implies: Corrects the baseline (VSS logged as 'Feb-2026, EUR 47m'): approval 14/01/2026, completion 30/01/2026, EUR 44m estimate, 350 leavers. 350 exits against a flat 244-branch Greek estate means the same counters must be run with fewer people - the classic driver for cash recyclers/TCRs, assisted self-service and branch automation.
signals.likelihood: Already executed; capability gap persists through 2026
signals.followup: Position recyclers/TCRs and teller-automation on a per-branch labour-substitution business case for the 244 Greek branches.

signals.signal: Impairment losses on fixed assets and equity investments jumped to EUR 52 million in 2025 (2024: EUR 13 million), 'mainly impairment losses for intangible assets for Euro 38 million that are no longer in use in the context of IT transformation activities'. Depreciation/amortisation fell to EUR 131 million (2024: EUR 174 million) partly because of that write-down; general and administrative expenses rose to EUR 345 million (2024: EUR 308 million) mainly on IT expenses and maintenance of IT equipment.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, results commentary
signals.implies: EUR 38m of software written off as no longer in use is hard evidence of legacy platforms actually being decommissioned and replaced, and rising IT-equipment maintenance spend is the running cost of an ageing device estate. Both are entry points for replacement hardware, software and managed maintenance.
signals.likelihood: Ongoing through the 2023-2026 strategic plan and its successor
signals.followup: Ask which application families were written off, and whether the IT-equipment maintenance line covers the ATM/APS estate.

signals.signal: Primary confirmation of the previously press-only channel split: digital channels (Web, Mobile, ATM, APS) carried 98% of total monetary transaction volume in 2025 versus 2% at the branch counter; e-Banking transactions +14% in number and +11% in value. Digital sales: 30% of retail products sold digitally, 78% of consumer loans disbursed digitally, 36% of debit cards issued online, 26% of new accounts opened through Retail Onboarding on myAlpha Mobile (eGov-KYC plus video-call identification). 'Upcoming support for ATM withdrawals via mobile devices' is listed as a planned accessibility/digital-wallet feature.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, 'Digital Banking' / 'Digital Sales' / 'Inclusive access'
signals.implies: Retires the baseline caveat that the 98%/2% split was unconfirmed. ATM and APS are counted inside the digital channel, so self-service is strategically protected rather than being run down. The stated plan for wallet/mobile-initiated ATM withdrawals is contactless/cardless ATM software work on Printec's incumbent estate, and 26% digital account opening with eGov-KYC keeps the eKYC/onboarding line live.
signals.likelihood: Cardless/wallet ATM withdrawal work in the next 12 months
signals.followup: Pitch cardless/QR/NFC wallet withdrawal on the existing contactless ATM base and tie it to the accessibility programme.

signals.signal: Alpha Bank Cyprus's 2025-27 Transformation Programme is running alongside the AstroBank operational merger: of 77 initiatives, 50 are complete, 16 in progress and 11 in the pipeline, and 16 flagship projects have been identified. Named priorities include the CRM platform, digital onboarding for individuals, companies AND international clients, Digital KYC Review, loan workflow automation, enhanced digital services via Alpha 360, payments platform optimisation and establishing an Automation Factory. Following the legal acquisition of AstroBank on 31/10/2025, system migration is the priority.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, 'International - Alpha Bank Cyprus'
signals.implies: An explicitly funded, itemised Cyprus programme naming digital onboarding, digital KYC review and payments-platform work - the core of Printec's eKYC/onboarding and payments offer - in a market where Printec Cyprus already services >26,000 POS and self-service/TCR estates. Corporate and international-client onboarding is the harder, higher-value eKYC segment.
signals.followup: Route through Printec Cyprus to the Alpha Bank Cyprus transformation office on digital onboarding for corporates/international clients and Digital KYC Review.

signals.signal: A new Group Retail Mobile app is in development with first launch scheduled Q4 2026 and full go-live targeted mid-2027, to deliver a unified Group digital experience; Alpha Bank London went live on a new Core Banking System with online banking completing in phases in Q1-Q2 2026 and a new debit card launching Q1 2026. The Digital Factory has grown to 15 agile squads.
signals.source_name: Alpha Bank Group Annual Report FY2025, 'International - Alpha Bank London' and 'Digital Transformation and Innovation Activities'
signals.implies: A Group-wide mobile replatforming with dated milestones pulls in identity/authentication, digital onboarding, card issuing and channel-integration work, and usually forces the self-service channel to be re-integrated to the new front end - a services attach point for the ATM/APS incumbent.
signals.likelihood: Committed dates: Q4 2026 first launch, mid-2027 full
signals.followup: Offer ATM/APS integration to the new Group mobile front end (cardless withdrawal, pre-staged transactions, wallet provisioning).
